newsitem.title: YEMEN: U.S. agency funds Yemen refinery feasibility study.
newsitem.headline: U.S. agency funds Yemen refinery feasibility study.

text.p: The U.S. Trade & Development Agency on Sunday signed an agreement with a Yemeni contracting firm to finance the feasibility study for a new oil refinery in the Arab state.

A USTDA press release said the $300,000 grant would fund the Ras Isa refinery project's final feasibility study as part of U.S. efforts to encourage private American investment in Yemen, one of the Arab world's poorest states.
The 120,000 barrels per day refinery, which marks the first time the private sector has been allowed in the downstream part of the oil industry, would cost about $800 million, the statement said.

The refinery would produce a range of petroleum products including gasoline, kerosene, jet fuel, diesel fuel, fuel oil and asphalt for the domestic and export market. It would be located at Ras Isa in Hudaidah province, 230 km (140 miles) west of Sanaa.
The country's only refinery, the Aden refinery, is more than 40 years old and was damaged in the 1994 civil war between north and south.
Yemen, a small independent oil producer, is trying to lure foreign investment.
